title: Why attention is O(n^2), and what Flash and Sage change

questions.q: You double an image's side at one token per latent cell. How much larger is the score matrix?
questions.why: Tokens go up 4 times, and the matrix goes with the square of tokens.

questions.q: What does slicing the queries change?
options: How much is held at once, not the answer
The answer, slightly, in exchange for memory
The number of tokens in the model
questions.answer: How much is held at once, not the answer
questions.why: Each slice is scored and dropped. The lab matches the full calculation to rounding error.

questions.q: Which of these is a different kind of bargain from the other two?
questions.why: The other two compute the same numbers in a different order. Rounding changes the numbers.

questions.q: On an NVIDIA card with PyTorch 2 and no attention flag, which backend does ComfyUI pick?
questions.why: model_management turns on pytorch attention by default there, and attention.py logs Using pytorch attention.

questions.q: Why does online softmax keep a running largest score?
options: To rescale earlier sums so the exponentials stay in range
To pick a single winning token
To skip tokens with low scores
questions.answer: To rescale earlier sums so the exponentials stay in range
questions.why: Each exponential is taken relative to the largest score so far, and earlier sums are corrected when it rises.

questions.q: How do you find out which backend you are really running?
options: Read the Using ... attention line in the console
Look at the file name of the model
It always matches the last flag you tried
questions.answer: Read the Using ... attention line in the console
questions.why: attention.py logs its choice at startup.
